name: kimi-memory
description: Three-layer local memory for Kimi Code (global user memory, per-project durable + working memory, per-project session archives) plus an integrated advisor subsystem for reflective prompts. Exposed via MCP tools, lifecycle hooks, and slash commands.
skillInstructions: Use the kimi-memory MCP tools. Routing rules: (1) durable facts about the user, their environment, or reusable workflows are GLOBAL — pass scope:'global' on memory_save so they land in $KIMI_CODE_HOME/kimi-memory/_global/memory.sqlite. (2) Durable facts about the active project (repo conventions, decisions, architectures) are PROJECT — default scope for memory_save/update/delete. (3) Transient current focus is working_memory_set/get/clear (project-only). (4) Session transcripts are conversation_list/get/search/ingest (project-only, automatic). memory_recall/list/get default to scope:'all' so a default caller sees project + global hits; pass scope:'project' or scope:'global' to filter. memory_similar and memory_conclusions_for also accept scope:'all' (project first, then global). Always pass `cwd` (the active project root), even for global writes — it stays as provenance context. Prefer memory_recall (scope:'all') before memory_save to avoid duplicates; if a recall hit exists, update or use supersede:true instead of saving a second copy. Use memory_link to write a typed edge between related memories, memory_merge to synthesize several rows into one, and memory_save with type:'conclusion' + synthesizes:[childIds] to record a higher-order synthesis. Use memory_reinforce after reading a recall hit so it stays fresh against decay. Echo the returned operation, scope, and id so the user can see what was persisted. Never store secrets (API keys, tokens, passwords, credentials, .env contents, PII). Advisor subsystem: when the UserPromptSubmit hook emits `[advisor] matched: "..."`, the prompt matched a reflection keyword — load skill `advisor` (or invoke /advisor) and follow the anchored-recommendation procedure. Do NOT push changes without the user's go-ahead. The advisor skill is loaded on demand; memory skill is loaded at SessionStart.

interface.shortDescription: Three-layer local memory plus a reflective advisor layer for Kimi Code.
interface.longDescription: Two subsystems: (1) Memory — a kimi-memory MCP server with four storage layers: GLOBAL durable memory at $KIMI_CODE_HOME/kimi-memory/_global/memory.sqlite (cross-project user preferences and reusable workflows); PROJECT durable + working memory at $KIMI_CODE_HOME/kimi-memory/<project-key>/memory.sqlite (repository facts and current focus); PROJECT session archives (conversations + conversation_events) ingested idempotently from Kimi's wire.jsonl; SHARED cross-project pool at $KIMI_CODE_HOME/kimi-memory/_shared/memory.sqlite (project_key='_shared') for ACL-promoted rows. (2) Advisor — a reflective-procedure skill that anchors on the active project and emits anchored recommendations.  Slash commands: /kimi-memory:list_memories, /kimi-memory:advisor, /kimi-memory:prune, /kimi-memory:reset-project, /kimi-memory:memos.  Tools (55): memory_save, memory_recall, memory_list, memory_get, memory_update, memory_delete, memory_save_bulk, memory_status, memory_similar, memory_link, memory_unlink, memory_edges, memory_merge, memory_conclusions_for, memory_parents, working_memory_set, working_memory_get, working_memory_clear, conversation_list, conversation_get, conversation_search, conversation_ingest, acl_grant, acl_revoke, acl_list, acl_share_memory, acl_resolve_principal, memory_set_tier, memory_promote, memory_demote, memory_tier_history, wiki_upsert_page, wiki_get_page, wiki_traverse, wiki_backlinks, wiki_resolve, codegraph_extract, codegraph_build_edges, codegraph_query_symbol, codegraph_impact_path, codegraph_callers, codegraph_callees, memory_prune, memory_reset_project, memory_diagnostics, dream_list_jobs, dream_get_job, dream_list_proposals, dream_get_proposal, dream_status, dream_enqueue, dream_generate_proposals, dream_apply_job, dream_discard_job.  Eight lifecycle hooks: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SessionEnd, PreCompact, Interrupt, StopFailure, PostToolUse. Recall output is structured (status line + per-memory list in hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext). Install via `/plugins install https://github.com/cbuntingde/kimi-memory`.
